Made by J.S. Henchman Forwarded by C Crawford

Vladimir Heger, Czechoslovakian, passport
No.27477 issued at Shanghai on June 22, 1935, was born
at Chotetov, Mlada Boleslav, on April 1st, 1901. After
completing primary and middle school training, he entered on
a military career but abandoning this a year or two later,
he decided to become a dentist and enrolled at the "Statni
Zubolikovsky Ustav" College at Prague. At the dental
school he failed to qualify as a dental surgeon, and is
therefore not authorised to use the title "doctor", but
managed to pass his examinations for laboratory dentist.
Until 1932, when he left for Egypt, Heger remained
in Czechoslovakia and during that period was convicted on
eight separate occasions on charges of false pretences,
misappropriation and embezzlement.
In Alexandria he bought a dental practice but
due to his lack of qualifications and the fact that part
of his history became known to Police was subsequently
forced to discontinue his activities and in August, 1933,
came to Shanghai.
Arriving in Shanghai he made the acquaintance of
practitioner
Dr. W. Korec, a medical/from whom he borrowed $3,000 Mex.
and in whose company and partnership he again began to
practise at 83 Peking Road.
Quarrelling with his partner over the repayment
of the loan, which loan never was repaid, Heger left him
and set up on his own on Nanking Road, obtaining the
necessary funds from a Mrs. Heister with whom he had
become more than casually friendly. Ferdinand Heister,
a German and the above mentioned lady's husband, was

弗拉基米尔·赫格，捷克斯洛伐克人，护照号码27477，1935年6月22日签发于上海，1901年4月1日出生于姆拉达-博莱斯拉夫（Mlada Boleslav）的霍特托夫（Chotetov）。在完成小学和中学教育后，他投身军旅，但一两年后放弃，决定成为一名牙医，并进入布拉格的“国立牙科研究所”（Statni Zubolikovsky Ustav）学院就读。在牙科学校期间，他未能取得牙科医师资格，因此无权使用“博士”头衔，但设法通过了实验室牙技师的考试。直到1932年前往埃及之前，赫格一直留在捷克斯洛伐克，在此期间，他因虚假借口、挪用公款和侵吞财产等罪名先后八次被判有罪。
在亚历山大港，他购买了一家牙科诊所，但由于缺乏资质，且其部分过往经历为警方所知，随后被迫停止活动，并于1933年8月来到上海。
抵达上海后，他结识了执业医师W. 科雷克（W. Korec）博士/医生，向其借款3,000墨西哥元，并与该人合伙，再次在北京路83号开始执业。
因偿还贷款问题与合伙人发生争执（该笔贷款从未偿还），赫格离开对方，在南京路独立开业，所需资金来自一位海斯特（Heister）夫人，他与该女士的关系已超出普通朋友范畴。费迪南德·海斯特（Ferdinand Heister），德国人，系上述女士的丈夫，当时在

On arrival in Shanghai he was arrested by the

fairly lengthy trial in which Mrs. Meister refused to
testify against him, Heger was found not guilty. Following
the trial a Miss Clara Barret, with whom he had been
friendly shortly after his first arrival in Shanghai,
brought charge of breach of promise against him. He was
also accused of obtaining $1,000 from the same lady.
Both these suits were, however, unsuccessful.

Wife Figures In Trial Of
Czechoslovakian Dentist

Mrs. F. Heister, who figured pro-
minently in the recent trial of Dr.
Vladimir Heger, who was accused
by her husband, F. Heister, of
stealing about $7,000 from his home
in the Embankment Building, yes-

At the time of the alleged gold
theft Mrs. Heister and Dr. Heger

Germany. However, before they
had gone far, Mr. Heister discover-

returned to Shanghai to stand

Mrs. Heister was released and
the case against her dropped.
However, the trial of Dr. Heger

which time two private criminal

which would damage his defense
in any way.

yesterday, Heister refused to agree

attorney served notice that he
would contest the charges. The

F. 海斯特夫人在近期捷克斯洛伐克牙医弗拉基米尔·赫格博士的审判中备受关注，赫格被其丈夫 F. 海斯特指控从其位于外滩大厦的家中窃取约7,000美元，昨日她以遭受极端残忍对待为由，对丈夫提起离婚诉讼。
在所谓的黄金盗窃发生时，海斯特夫人和赫格博士正计划离开上海前往德国。然而，在他们尚未走远时，海斯特先生发现了所谓的损失，并将两人追回上海受审。
海斯特夫人被释放，针对她的案件被撤销。
然而，赫格博士的审判持续了近两个月，在此期间，两起私人刑事案件对他提起诉讼。他在所有三起案件中均被判无罪。
在整个赫格博士的审判过程中，海斯特夫人是一名感兴趣的旁观者，虽然她作为控方证人出庭，但她拒绝提供任何可能损害其辩护的证词。
当昨天提交申请时，海斯特拒绝同意分居，并通过其律师发出通知，表示将对指控进行抗辩。该案将在第一特区地方法院审理。
海斯特夫人由保罗·普雷梅特代理，海斯特先生由罗先生代理。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, APRIL 13, 1935.

DR. HEGER ACQUITTED
IN THIRD CASE
Czech Dentist Found Not
Guilty Of Breach Of
Promise

Dr. Vladimir Heger, 34, Czech,
dentist, who had spent the better
part of the last six weeks between
the First Special District Court
and the Amoy Road Gaol, was
finally made a free man yester-
day afternoon when he was ac-
quitted of the private criminal
prosecution involving a breach of
promise suit brought against him
by Miss Clara Barret.

On Tuesday last after a trial
and a re-trial lasting since Feb-
ruary 22, Dr. Heger was acquitted
by the criminal court of the
charge of having stolen $7,399
worth of gold bars and notes from
the apartment of Mr. F. Heister,
German, residing in the Embank-
ment building. A few weeks prior
to that a private criminal prosecu-
tion charging Dr. Heger with
having taken by deceit two dia-
mond rings from Mrs. Heiter,
was dismissed.

It will be remembered that Dr.
Heger left Shanghai for Dairen
and then Harbin on January 10,
last. He was then accompanied
by Mrs. Heister and her little
daughter. Mr. Heister, however,
with the assistance of the Shang-
hai Municipal Police, telegraphed
to Tsingtao, had his wife and
child stopped and returned to him.
Dr. Heger proceeded to Harbin,
then made his way to Japan,
where he was arrested and deport-
ed here as an "undesirable alien."
Dr. Heger was represented by
Mr. Paul Premet, M. D. Shikis
and Ngay Tchang-ling in all the
three cases.

赫格博士在第三起案件中
被判无罪
捷克牙医被发现
无罪释放
违背婚约案

34岁的捷克牙医弗拉基米尔·赫格博士，在过去六周的大部分时间里穿梭于第一特区地方法院和厦门路监狱之间，昨日下午终于恢复自由，他在克拉拉·巴雷特小姐对他提起的涉及违背婚约的私人刑事公诉中被判无罪。

上周二，经过自2月22日开始的审判和重审，赫格博士被刑事法庭宣判无罪，免除其从居住在外滩大厦的德国人 F. 海斯特先生公寓中盗窃价值7,399美元的金条和钞票的指控。在此之前几周，一起指控赫格博士通过欺骗手段从海特（Heiter）夫人处拿走两枚钻石戒指的私人刑事诉讼被驳回。

值得一提的是，赫格博士于去年1月10日离开上海前往大连，随后前往哈尔滨。当时海斯特夫人和她的小女儿与他同行。然而，海斯特先生在上海公共租界工部局警务处的协助下，向青岛发电报，拦回其妻儿并归还给他。赫格博士前往哈尔滨，随后辗转至日本，在那里被捕并以“不受欢迎的外国人”身份被驱逐至此。
在所有三起案件中，赫格博士均由保罗·普雷梅特先生、M. D. 希基斯（M. D. Shikis）和 Ngai Tchang-ling（音译）代表。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 10, 1935

Dr. V. Heger Is Acquitted
On Theft Charge

Czech Dentist Is Found Not Guilty After Re-trial;
Released On Security During Appeal; Judgment
In Breach Of Promise Suit Due On Friday

Dr. Vladimir Heger, 34-year-old Czech dentist, whose deportation from Japan as an "undesirable alien" and subsequent arrest and trial on a charge of having stolen $7,390 worth of gold bars and currency from the apartment of Mr. F. Heister, German, residing in the Embankment building, had been followed with interest, was acquitted by Judge Shiang in the First Special District Court after a trial which commenced on February 22, last and a re-trial which was concluded last Wednesday.

Although acquitted on the charge of theft, Dr. Heger was ordered to provide the original security of $500, during the period of appeal. The bail was lowered to $500 bond at the last hearing held on April 2, upon strong representations of Mr. Paul Premet, who defended the Czech dentist, together with Mr. M. D. Shikis and Mr. Ngai Tchen-ling.

Arrested In Tokyo

Since the receipt here of the Rengo dispatch from Tokyo dated February 13, which stated that Dr. Heger was being held there as an alleged head of a "white slave" organization operating in Japan and China ports, Dr. Heger has proved a source of interest for the local community. Then, a few days later, it was revealed by the Shanghai Municipal Police that the dentist was wanted here on a charge of allegedly having robbed Mr. Heister of $7,390 in gold bars and currency.

Dr. Heger was accordingly deported from Japan and upon arrival here, on February 21, he was handed over to officers of the Hongkew Police Station and the following day was arraigned before the First Special District Court on a charge of larceny.

During the course of the trial and the re-trial, which lasted many hearings the following story was unfolded: It was disclosed that Dr. Heger arrived in Shanghai about August, 1933, and with the help of another dentist he opened an office. Mr. Heister, the complainant in the case, and Mrs. Heister as well as their little daughter, were his patients.

Ran Away With Mrs. Heister

Later, apparently, Dr. Heger and Mrs. Heister were on very friendly terms and on January 10, they ran away together, accompanied by Mrs. Heister's daughter, to Tsingtao. Mr. Heister did not discover that his wife was missing until that afternoon and then heard that she had departed with Dr. Heger and his little daughter. It was only then that he suspected that his gold bars, which he kept in a cabinet in his apartment, might have been stolen. He looked and found them missing.

He immediately reported the matter to the Shanghai Municipal Police, who wired to Tsingtao, and Mrs. Heister and her little daughter were taken off the boat and returned to Shanghai. Dr. Heger, however, it is understood proceeded to Harbin and from there went to Japan, where he was arrested and deported as an "undesirable alien."

During the trial Mr. Heister alleged that no one except Dr. Heger could have stolen his money. He stated that his wife could not have taken it, as if she did, she would have left something for him. Little incriminating evidence except Mr. Heister's allegations, was produced at the trial against Dr. Heger, while, on his behalf, Mr. Premet produced a great deal of evidence.

Dr. Heger stated that he had never visited Mr. Heister's apartment in the Embankment Building. His story was backed up by the house-boy employed by Mr. Heister, who stated that he had never seen Dr. Heger in the apartment.

There is still a private criminal prosecution on a breach of promise suit hanging over the Czech dentist. He is being charged under Article 244 of the Chinese Criminal Code by Miss Clara Barret, who alleges that he promised to marry her. Judgment in this case will be handed down in the First Special District Court on Friday afternoon.

《字林西报》，1935年4月10日，星期三

V. 黑格博士被宣告无罪
盗窃指控不成立

捷克牙医在重审后被裁定无罪；
上诉期间获准保释；
违背婚约诉讼判决将于周五下达

34岁的捷克牙医弗拉基米尔·黑格（Vladimir Heger）博士，此前因被日本作为“不受欢迎的外国人”驱逐出境，随后又因涉嫌从居住在堤岸大厦（Embankment building）的德国人F. 海斯特（F. Heister）先生公寓内窃取价值7,390美元的金条和货币而被捕受审，此事一直备受关注。经过去年2月22日开始的首次审判以及上周三结束的重审，第一特区法院的项法官（Judge Shiang）裁定黑格博士无罪。

尽管盗窃罪名不成立，但黑格博士仍被责令在上诉期间提供原定的500美元担保。在4月2日举行的最后一次听证会上，鉴于为这位捷克牙医辩护的保罗·普雷梅特（Paul Premet）律师，连同M. D. 希基斯（M. D. Shikis）先生和魏振灵（Ngai Tchen-ling）先生的强烈陈情，保释金被减至500美元具结保释。

在东京被捕

自2月13日收到来自东京的联合通讯社（Rengo）电报以来，黑格博士便成为本地社区关注的焦点。该电报称，黑格博士因涉嫌担任一个在日本和中国港口活动的“白奴”组织头目而在当地被拘留。随后几天，上海公共租界工部局警务处披露，该牙医在此地亦被通缉，涉嫌抢劫海斯特先生价值7,390美元的金条和货币。

因此，黑格博士被日本驱逐出境。2月21日抵达上海后，他被移交给虹口捕房的警官，并于次日在第一特区法院以盗窃罪被提审。

在持续多次听证的审判和重审过程中，案情逐渐明朗：据披露，黑格博士于1933年8月左右抵达上海，并在另一位牙医的帮助下开设了诊所。本案原告海斯特先生、海斯特夫人及其小女儿均为他的病人。

与海斯特夫人私奔

后来，黑格博士与海斯特夫人显然关系非常亲密，1月10日，两人偕同海斯特夫人的女儿一起逃往青岛。海斯特先生直到当天下午才发现妻子失踪，随后得知她已与黑格博士及他的小女儿一同离去。直到此时，他才怀疑自己存放在公寓橱柜里的金条可能被盗。经查看，发现金条确实不见了。

他立即向上海公共租界工部局警务处报案，警方随即致电青岛，海斯特夫人及其小女儿被拦下并遣返上海。然而，据悉黑格博士前往哈尔滨，并从那里去了日本，在那里他被捕并被作为“不受欢迎的外国人”驱逐出境。

在审判期间，海斯特先生声称，除了黑格博士外，不可能有其他人偷走他的钱。他表示，他的妻子不可能拿走钱，因为如果真是她拿的，她会给他留一些。除海斯特先生的指控外，庭审中针对黑格博士提出的不利证据寥寥无几，而普雷梅特先生则代表被告方提供了大量证据。

黑格博士声称，他从未去过海斯特先生在堤岸大厦的公寓。这一说法得到了海斯特先生雇佣的男仆的佐证，该男仆表示他从未在公寓里见过黑格博士。

目前，这位捷克牙医仍面临一起关于违背婚约的私人刑事起诉。克拉拉·巴雷特（Clara Barret）小姐依据《中华民国刑法》第244条对他提出指控，声称他曾许诺娶她。该案判决将于周五下午在第一特区法院宣布。

（批注：档案号 9/4 1935）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, MARCH 28, 1935
10301.

Dr. V. Heger Alleges Charge
Against Him Framed

Czech Dentist Alleges Mr. Heister Wanted To Get
Wife Back And Therefore Instigated Charge
To Stop Her; $500 Bail Is Fixed

The re-trial of Dr. Vladimir
Heger, 34, Czechoslovakian
dentist, charged with stealing
$7,390 worth of gold and cur-
rency from the apartment of Mr.
F. Heister, German, residing in
the Embankment building, was
opened before Judge Shiang in
the First Special District Court
yesterday morning. After a
fairly lengthy hearing, at the
close of which Dr. Heger stated
that Mr. Heister had instigated
the charge against him in order
to get his wife back and that
now he had to go through with
it, Judge Shiang adjourned the
session until next Tuesday,
April 2.

Following a heated applica-
tion made on behalf of Dr.
Heger by his attorney, Mr. Paul
Premet, the Czech dentist was
allowed to be released on $500
bail, instead of the original sum
of $7,390 fixed by the judge at
the opening of the case.

In accordance with the instruc-
tions of the court made at the
previous hearing the Police,
under the direction of Dr. Heger,
located the chauffeur of the Lee
Lee Garage, who drove the ac-
cused to the Embankment build-
ing on North. Soochow Road on
the morning of January 9, when
Mrs. Heister left with the dentist
and her 10-year-old daughter,
Louisa. The chauffeur stated
that he had driven up to en-
trance "C," while Dr. Heger and
Mrs. Heister maintained that it
was entrance "D." The chauffeur
then stated that he only took
one trunk, while the accused had
previously stated that it was
three trunks.

Boy Testifies

The next witness was the boy
employed by Mr. Heister in his
apartment. He stated that he
was in the flat on the morning
of January 9, but did not see
the accused come in. He denied
ever seeing Dr. Heger before. In
closing his evidence the boy
stated that he only heard of the
theft of the gold bars about
three weeks after January 9.

Louisa, the little daughter of
Mr. and Mrs. Heister was then
placed in the witness stand and
in a clear voice said that she
knew Dr. Heger, as he had
pulled her teeth. On January 9,
she said she sailed together with
him and her mother to Tsingtao,
but she did so, she added, be-
cause her mama asked her to go
along. She denied having ever
seen Dr. Heger in their apart-
ment.

Wife Not Suspected

Mr. Heister the complainant,
was then told to take the wit-
ness stand and was asked by
the Judge how he discovered the
theft. He stated that on the
morning of January 10, he dis-
covered that his wife was miss-
ing. He did not suspect her of
the theft; in fact, he did not know
of the theft then. However,
later he found out that she had
run away with the accused to
Tsingtao, and then upon check-
ing he found that his gold was
gone, and it was then, he relat-
ed, that he suspected Dr. Heger.

Mr. Heister added that his
wife had gone to see Dr. F. Wil-
helm on January 4, and asked
his advice whether she could
take her husband's money. Dr.
Wilhelm had told her that it was
illegal.

"Why don't you suspect your
wife?" questioned Judge Shiang.

"Because my wife would not
have taken all my money; she
would have left something for
me," answered Mr. Heister.

"You don't suspect that your
wife shared the money with Dr.
Heger?"

"No. Dr. Heger took it all."

Judge Shiang then questioned
Mrs. Heister, "You said that you
came down with four trunks?
The chauffeur says that there
was only one?"

"I cannot help that," answered
the woman, "I remember per-
fectly well how much baggage I
had, as I put it myself into the
car."

At this stage the hearing was
adjourned until Tuesday morning
and Dr. Heger was granted bail
at $500.

Mr. M. Shikis and Mr. Ngai
Tchon-ling are associated with
Mr. Premet in defending Dr.
Heger.

V. 黑格博士声称
针对他的指控系捏造

捷克牙医声称海斯特先生为了挽回妻子而唆使提出指控以阻止她离开；保释金定为500美元

昨天上午，第一特区法院项法官（Judge Shiang）开庭重审34岁捷克斯洛伐克牙医弗拉基米尔·黑格（Vladimir Heger）博士一案，他被控从居住在堤岸大厦的德国人F. 海斯特先生公寓内窃取价值7,390美元的金条和货币。经过相当长时间的听证，黑格博士在听证结束时表示，海斯特先生为了挽回妻子而唆使对他提出指控，而他现在不得不应对这一局面。随后，项法官宣布休庭，直至下周二，即4月2日。

在黑格博士的律师保罗·普雷梅特（Paul Premet）先生提出激烈的申请后，法庭允许这位捷克牙医以500美元保释金获释，而非案件开始时法官确定的原定金额7,390美元。

按照上次听证时法庭的指示，警方在黑格博士的指引下，找到了利利车行（Lee Lee Garage）的司机，该司机曾在1月9日上午将被告载至北苏州路的堤岸大厦，当时海斯特夫人随同牙医及其10岁的女儿路易莎（Louisa）离开。司机表示，他将车开到了“C”入口，而黑格博士和海斯特夫人则坚持说是“D”入口。司机随后表示，他只搬运了一个行李箱，而被告此前声称是三个行李箱。

男仆作证

下一位证人是海斯特先生公寓雇佣的男仆。他表示，1月9日上午他在公寓内，但没有看到被告进来。他否认以前见过黑格博士。在结束证言时，男仆表示，他是在1月9日大约三周后才听说金条被盗一事。

随后，海斯特夫妇的小女儿路易莎出庭作证，她用清晰的声音说，她认识黑格博士，因为他曾为她拔牙。她说，1月9日她与黑格博士及母亲一同乘船前往青岛，但她补充说，她之所以这样做，是因为妈妈让她一起去。她否认曾在他们的公寓里见过黑格博士。

妻子未受怀疑

随后，原告海斯特先生被传唤出庭，法官询问他是如何发现盗窃案的。他表示，1月10日上午，他发现妻子失踪了。他并未怀疑她盗窃；事实上，当时他并不知道发生了盗窃。然而，后来他发现她与被告一起逃往青岛，经检查发现他的金子不见了，他说，就在那时他开始怀疑黑格博士。

海斯特先生补充说，他的妻子曾在1月4日去见F. 威廉（F. Wilhelm）博士，咨询她是否可以拿走丈夫的钱。威廉博士告诉她这是非法的。

“你为什么不怀疑你的妻子？”项法官问道。

“因为我的妻子不会拿走我所有的钱；她会给我留一些的，”海斯特先生回答。

“你不怀疑你的妻子与黑格博士分赃吗？”

“不。是黑格博士全拿走了。”

随后，项法官讯问海斯特夫人：“你说你带了四个行李箱下来？司机说只有一个？”

“那我也没办法，”这位女士回答，“我记得很清楚我有多少行李，因为是我亲自把它们放进车里的。”

至此，听证会休庭至周二上午，黑格博士获准以500美元保释。

Judge Orders Dr. Heger's
Trial Be Re-opened

Jurist Doesn't Pronounce Judgment As Expected,
Wants Two Points Cleared; Police Clear
One; Hearing Adjourned To March 27

Instead of pronouncing judgment upon Dr. Vladimir Heger, 34, Czechoslovakian dentist, charged with stealing $7,390 worth of gold and currency from the apartment of Mr. F. Heister, German, residing in the Embankment building, as he was expected to do, Judge Shiang presiding over the case in the First Special District Court yesterday morning ordered the case to be re-opened. The re-trial being set for next Wednesday.

After eight lengthy hearings the court still seemed in doubt on two points. Judge Shiang wanted to know whether the key Dr. Heger was seen making about a fortnight prior to the discovery of the theft, was actually a key to his letter box as he alleged. The prosecution answered this question, pointing out that the police had investigated on this point and found that Dr. Heger was telling the truth.

The second point on which the court was not clear was whether on January 9, last (the day on which Dr. Heger left Shanghai for Dairen accompanied by Mrs. Heister and her little daughter), he entered the Heister flat in the Embankment apartments, when Mrs. Heister was taking her trunks out, or as he had already told the court he had only awaited her in the hall on the ground floor.

On this point Judge Shiang then commenced questioning Dr. Heger at length.

Q.—Where did you get the taxi in which you went to pick up Mrs. Heister? What was the name of the garage.

A.—From a garage on North Honan Road, just opposite the Embankment Building.

Q.—Did you sign a chit there?

A.—I didn't sign anything. I paid cash.

Q.—Could you find the garage and recognize the chauffeur?

A.—Undoubtedly I can find the garage, but I am not sure that I could recognize the chauffeur.

Q.—Up to what entrance did you drive in the taxi and did you go upstairs?

In reply Dr. Heger showed the entrance on the plan of the building and said, that he didn't go upstairs, because Mrs. Heister's luggage had already been brought down in the elevator. From the hall the trunks were put into the car by the chauffeur, Dr. Heger concluded.

Judge Shiang continued the questioning on the same issue for a considerable time and then adjourned the hearing until next Wednesday morning, March 27. The prosecution at the conclusion of the case asked the police to bring Mr. Heister's cook to testify at the next hearing.

Apart from the criminal action of theft on which Dr. Heger is being tried, there have been two civil actions filed against him by Mr. Heister.

Mr. Paul Premet is appearing on behalf of Dr. Heger together with Mr. M. Shikis and Mr. Ngai Tchon-ling.

法官命令重审赫格医生案

法官未按预期宣判，要求澄清两点；警方澄清其中一点；听证会休庭至3月27日

昨天上午，在第一特区法院主持该案的尚法官（Judge Shiang）并未如预期那样对现年34岁、被控从居住在百老汇大厦（Embankment building）的德国人F. 海斯特（F. Heister）先生公寓中窃取价值7,390美元黄金和货币的捷克斯洛伐克牙医弗拉基米尔·赫格（Vladimir Heger）博士进行宣判，而是命令重开此案。重审定于下周三进行。

经过八次漫长的听证，法庭在两点上似乎仍存疑。尚法官想知道，赫格博士在被发现盗窃前约两周被人看到配制的那把钥匙，是否真如他所称是其信箱的钥匙。检方回答了这个问题，指出警方已就此点进行调查，并发现赫格博士所言属实。

法庭不清楚的第二点是，在去年1月9日（即赫格博士在海斯特夫人及其小女儿陪同下离开上海前往大连的那天），当海斯特夫人将她的皮箱搬出时，他是否进入了百老汇公寓的海斯特寓所，还是像他此前向法庭陈述的那样，仅在一楼大厅等候她。

就这一点，尚法官随即开始详细讯问赫格博士。

问.—你去接海斯特夫人时所乘的出租车是从哪里叫的？车行的名称是什么？

答.—从河南北路的一个车行，就在百老汇大厦正对面。

问.—你在那里签单了吗？

答.—我没签任何东西。我付的是现金。

问.—你能找到那家车行并认出司机吗？

答.—我无疑能找到那家车行，但我不确定能认出司机。

问.—你们坐出租车到了哪个入口，你上楼了吗？

赫格博士作为回答，在建筑平面图上指出了入口，并说他没有上楼，因为海斯特夫人的行李已经由电梯运了下来。赫格博士总结说，皮箱是从大厅由司机装入车内的。

尚法官就同一问题继续讯问了相当长的时间，随后宣布听证会休庭，直至下周三（3月27日）上午。案件结束时，检方要求警方传唤海斯特先生的厨子在下次听证会上作证。

除了赫格博士正在受审的盗窃刑事案件外，海斯特先生还对他提起了两起民事诉讼。

保罗·普雷梅特（Paul Premet）先生与M. 希基斯（M. Shikis）先生及魏宗灵（Ngai Tchon-ling，音译）先生一同代表赫格博士出庭。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MARCH 16, 1935
Heger Hearings
Ended Before
District Court
Czech Dentist To Learn
Fate Friday; Charge Of
Theft Left To Judge

After eight spectacular sessions
the trial of Dr. Vladimir Heger,
34, Czechoslovakian dentist, was
brought to a close yesterday morn-
ing in the First Special District
when he was remanded until next
Friday for judgment. He is accus-
ed of stealing $7,390 from the
apartment of Mr. F. Heister in the
Embarkment Building.
Dr. Heger and Mrs. Heister, the
wife of the complaining witness,
were arrested while en route to
Germany with the Heister's five-
year old daughter. He was return-
ed to Shanghai from Japan to
stand trial. Mrs. Heister, it was
generally hinted, would prove to be
the most damaging witness for the
prosecution.
The case had all of the elements
of a modern four-star flicker with
Mrs. Heister enshrouded in mys-
tery.

Suit Dropped
However, as the case against
Heger progressed it became increas-
ingly evident that Mrs. Heister
would not offer any evidence
which would damage the case of
the man with whom she started
her flight to Germany.
Although she signed a private
criminal prosecution suit against
Heger for the return of two dia-
mond rings, she would not proceed
with the criminal aspect of the
case and announced herself as in-
terested in the return of the rings
only. This suit was subsequently
dropped.
Witnesses have been produced
throughout the trial tending to
show that Dr. Heger was not parti-
cularly interested in paying his
bills promptly. Further, that he
commercialized his love affairs to
some extent.
Heister, the irate husband, has
throughout the trial bent every
effort to assist the prosecution. He
lost over $7,000 and saw his wife
flee with the man he believes stole
his money. On the witness stand
he testified that Dr. Heger had
treated him roughly when he
(Heister) was a dental patient of
Heger's. His head was pulled back
so hard, he testified, that he be-
came semi-conscious. It was then,
he believes, that Heger took the
key to his lock-box and drained its
contents preparatory to his intend-
ed flight to Germany.

Appears Nonchalant
A surprise witness was offered
during the trial in the person of
Miss Clara Barat who testified that
Dr. Heger had made love to her
and had subsequently borrowed
her money. She testified that so
far she has not been re-paid. He
also has a watch belonging to her,
she says. Miss Barat is contem-
plating private proceedings against
Dr. Heger for the return of her
money and timepiece.
Dr. Heger appeared in court yes-
terday well groomed and wearing
a new suit of clothes. He does not
show any signs of anguish from his
days in jail.
Dr. Heger and Mrs. Heister con-
tinued to pass furtive yet under-
standing glances at each other
yesterday, he from the prisoner's
dock and she from her seat along-
side her husband who continues to
be less appreciative of Heger's
plight than his spouse. Miss Barat
was not in court yesterday.

经过八次引人注目的庭审，现年34岁的捷克斯洛伐克牙医弗拉基米尔·赫格博士的审判于昨天上午在第一特区法院结束，他被还押候审，直至下周五宣判。他被指控从百老汇大厦（Embarkment Building，原文拼写有误，应为Embankment）F. 海斯特先生的公寓中窃取7,390美元。

赫格博士与投诉证人之妻海斯特夫人以及海斯特夫妇五岁的女儿在前往德国的途中被捕。他从日本被引渡回上海受审。普遍暗示，海斯特夫人将成为对检方最有利的证人。

本案具备现代四星电影的所有元素，海斯特夫人笼罩在神秘之中。

撤诉
然而，随着针对赫格的案件进展，越来越明显的是，海斯特夫人不会提供任何损害那个与她一同开始逃亡德国的男人的案件的证据。
尽管她签署了一份针对赫格的私人刑事起诉诉状，要求归还两枚钻戒，但她不愿推进该案的刑事方面，并宣布自己只关心戒指的归还。随后该诉讼被撤销。
在整个审判过程中，提供的证人倾向于表明赫格博士并不特别热衷于及时支付账单。此外，他在某种程度上将他的风流韵事商业化。

愤怒的丈夫海斯特在整个审判过程中竭尽全力协助检方。他损失了超过7,000美元，并目睹妻子与他认为偷了他钱的人私奔。在证人席上，他作证说，当他（海斯特）是赫格的牙科病人时，赫格对待他很粗暴。他作证说，他的头被用力向后拉，以至于他变得半昏迷。他认为，就在那时，赫格拿走了他保险箱的钥匙，并掏空了里面的东西，为他打算逃往德国做准备。

显得漫不经心
克拉拉·巴拉特（Clara Barat）小姐作为意外证人在审判期间出庭，作证说赫格博士曾向她求爱，并随后借了她的钱。她作证说，到目前为止她尚未收到还款。她说，他还有一块属于她的手表。巴拉特小姐正考虑对赫格博士提起私人诉讼，以追回她的钱款和手表。

赫格博士昨天出庭时衣着整洁，穿着一套新西装。他在狱中度过的日子并没有让他表现出任何痛苦的迹象。

昨天，赫格博士和海斯特夫人继续互相传递隐秘但心领神会的眼神，他从被告席，她从坐在丈夫旁边的座位，而她的丈夫对赫格的困境远不如他的配偶那样同情。巴拉特小姐昨天未出庭。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 6, 1935.

Dentist Tells
About Heger's
Local Practice

Heister Brings In Girl To
Show Defendant Took
Her Money, Didn't Repay

The trial of Dr. Vladimir Heger,
34-year-old Czechoslovakian dentist
charged with theft, was continued
before Judge Shing in the First
Special District Court yesterday
and after nearly two hours of hear-
ing evidence the accused was re-
manded to jail sine die.

The first witness called by the
prosecution was Dr. W. Korec, who
testified that he had given Dr.
Heger a room in the former's
office in which to practice dentistry
and that he had loaned him money
on various occasions. He also had
guaranteed a substantial amount
with a supply firm for Heger's in-
struments and equipment. The
total amount Dr. Heger owed him,
he testified, is about Tls. 3,000. It
is still outstanding, he claims. Dr.
Heger testified that the major
part of the loan and guarantee
which Dr. Korec had posted had
been relieved by two promissory
notes which he had given the wit-
ness. Dr. Korec testified that
Heger had made a "good living"
while he practiced but that shortly
before his attempted flight to Ger-
many with Mrs. F. Heister and her
baby daughter he had become lax
in keeping office hours and conse-
quently his earnings had fallen off
sharply.

Not Nearly Enough

Dr. Heger and Mrs. Heister had
previously testified that he had ap-
proximately $1,700 when the trip
was undertaken. When asked by
the judge yesterday why he had
not paid his debts with the amount
instead of attempting flight he

said, "Oh! There was not nearly
enough to pay my debts."

Mr. F. Heister, the complainant
witness in the action, followed Dr.
Korec to the witness stand and
testified shortly that he wished to
present a new witness for the pro-
secution. The new angle proved to
be Miss Clara Baral, who had
known Dr. Heger, according to her
testimony, not too long but enough
as well.

She said the accused had borrow-
ed $150 from her which had not
been repaid. He also had proposed
marriage to her and promised to
take her to Elysian bliss in Alex-
andria where he had a growing
business. His proposal, she said
was turned down. Because of her
loan to Dr. Heger she had been
penniless and although she had
asked him to return the money on
several occasions, she still was a
creditor of Dr. Heger's in the ori-
ginal amount of $150.

Mrs. Heister was the last witness
called for the prosecution. She
merely reiterated her previous evi-
dence regarding the date and time
she had first acquainted Dr. Heger
with the fact that her husband had
a quantity of gold in their apart-
ment.

Throughout the session yesterday
Dr. Heger maintained a distinct
aloofness and only when reference
was made to the alleged theft did
his calm disappear.

执业情况

海斯特带出一名女孩以
显示被告拿了她的钱
未予偿还

现年34岁、被控盗窃的捷克斯洛伐克牙医弗拉基米尔·赫格博士的审判，昨天在尚法官（Judge Shing，音译，应指前文之Shiang）主持的第一特区法院继续进行，经过近两小时的证据听证，被告被无限期还押监狱。

检方传唤的第一位证人是W. 科雷克（W. Korec）博士，他作证说，他曾在他自己的办公室里给赫格博士提供一个房间用于牙科执业，并曾多次借钱给他。他还为赫格的器械和设备向一家供应公司担保了一大笔款项。他作证说，赫格博士欠他的总金额约为3,000两白银。他声称这笔钱仍未偿还。赫格博士作证说，科雷克博士提供的贷款和担保的大部分，已通过他给证人开具的两张本票得以解除。科雷克博士作证说，赫格在执业期间过着“富裕的生活”，但在不久之前，当他试图与F. 海斯特夫人及其幼女逃往德国时，他在遵守办公时间方面变得松懈，因此收入急剧下降。

远远不够

赫格博士和海斯特夫人此前曾作证说，在启程时他手头约有1,700美元。当法官昨天问他为何不用这笔钱偿还债务而不是试图逃跑时，

他说：“哦！那远远不足以偿还我的债务。”

本案的原告证人F. 海斯特先生紧随科雷克博士之后走上证人席，并简短作证说他希望为检方提供一名新证人。新的角度结果是克拉拉·巴拉尔（Clara Baral，音译，前文为Barat）小姐，据她作证，她认识赫格博士的时间不算太长，但也足够了解。

她说被告向她借了150美元，尚未偿还。他还向她求婚，并承诺带她去亚历山大港享受极乐世界，他在那里有一家日益发展的企业。她说，她的求婚被拒绝了。因为借给赫格博士钱，她身无分文，虽然她多次要求他还钱，但她仍然是赫格博士的债权人，金额仍为最初的150美元。

海斯特夫人是检方传唤的最后一名证人。她只是重申了她之前的证词，关于她首次告知赫格博士其丈夫在公寓中藏有大量黄金的日期和时间。

在昨天的整个庭审过程中，赫格博士保持着明显的冷漠态度，只有当提及所谓的盗窃时，他的冷静才消失。

Wife Tells
About Flight
To Tsingtao
Czech Dentist, German
Face Each Other During
Theft Trial As Story
Of Romances Unfolded
Heger Denies Gold Theft;
Released On $7,390 Bail
Mrs. Heister, blond German wife
of Mr. F. Heister, complaining wit-
ness against Dr. Vladimir Heger, 37,
Czechoslovakian dentist, who is
accused of stealing $7,390 from
Heister, was the first witness called
when the case against Dr. Heger
was continued yesterday in Judge
Shiang's court in the settlement
Chinese tribunal. After nearly two
hours of testimony Dr. Heger was
released upon posting $7,390 bail,
the amount which he is accused of
appropriating from Heister.
Mrs. Heister's testimony, which it
was generally believed would clinch
the prosecution case against Dr.
Heger, failed in this respect.
Although she was closely question-
ed regarding her knowledge of Dr.
Heger's movements prior to the
time he is accused of stealing the
Heister valuables, she was unable
to give any material aid to the pro-
secution.
Hostility Evident
There was a marked air of mutual
grievance between the three actors
in the triangular drama as Mrs.
Heister took the witness stand. Dr.
Heger, not six feet away, seemed
to be fighting an urge to publicly
denounce his former friend while
her husband sallied back and forth
between his courtroom seat and the
witness stand lending moral and
legal support to the witness, at the
same time giving savage side glances
at the prisoner.
Mrs. Heister testified that she
had known Dr. Heger for about one
year; that she had seen him often
and that they had decided to go
to Germany together. They were
taking her baby daughter with
them. Dr. Heger was to pay for
the trip. Although she was ques-
tioned at length whether or not Dr.
Heger had access to her husband's
gold depository, a fact which if
proved would have unquestionably
convicted the accused dentist, she
steadfastly refused to make a con-
crete statement which would im-
plicate Dr. Heger. The importance
of her testimony failed to materia-
lize and after a series of routine
questions regarding her proposed
trip to Germany with Dr. Heger
and her arrest at Tsingtao and
subsequent removal here, she was
excused.
Roughed In Chair
Her husband followed her to the
witness stand and testified that Dr.
Heger had "treated him badly"
when he was a patient of the ac-
cused. At one time, he said, while
in the process of molding a dental
form, Dr. Heger had thrown back
his head with such force that he
had swooned and "believed" he was
in a semi-conscious condition. It
was at this time, he testified, that
Dr. Heger, he believed, had taken
the key to his strong box and
later removed its contents prepara-
tory to his flight to Germany with
the woman and child.
Later, Heister showed the degree
of pitch to which the case had
urged him, when in a verbal tilt
with Heger's attorney he heatedly
denied that "the entire case is a
family quarrel and has no place in
a court of law."
It was plainly evident throughout
the proceedings yesterday that the
prosecution hung upon proof that
Dr. Heger had been in possession
of the key to Heister's strong box
and that he modeled a duplicate
with which he made the illegal
entry. However, every attempt to
get a concrete statement from the
witnesses that would prove the
point failed. A Chinese servant or
an intimate of Heister also failed
to seal Heger's doom when it de-
veloped that all he could testify
to was the fact that he had seen
the accused with a "key."
Police investigation had previous-
ly proved that Dr. Heger was re-
making a key to his post office box
when seen by the boy. The case
was called for continuance on
March 5.

赫格否认盗窃黄金；

海斯特先生（Mr. F. Heister）的金发德国籍妻子海斯特夫人，作为指控37岁的捷克斯洛伐克牙医弗拉基米尔·赫格博士（Dr. Vladimir Heger）从海斯特处窃取7,390美元的控方证人，是昨日在公共租界华界法庭向法官香（Shiang，音译）继续审理赫格博士案件时传唤的第一位证人。经过近两个小时的作证，赫格博士在缴纳7,390美元保释金后获释，该金额即被指控其从海斯特处侵吞的数额。
海斯特夫人的证词原本被普遍认为将坐实针对赫格博士的检方指控，但在这方面并未如愿。
尽管就其在被指控窃取海斯特贵重物品之前对赫格博士行踪的了解情况受到了严密盘问，但她未能向检方提供任何实质性的帮助。
敌意显露
当海斯特夫人走上证人席时，这出三角戏剧中的三位主角之间弥漫着明显的相互怨怼气氛。赫格博士就在不到六英尺远的地方，似乎正在努力克制公开谴责这位昔日朋友的冲动；而她的丈夫则在法庭座位和证人席之间来回走动，为证人提供精神和法律支持，同时向被告投去凶狠的侧目。
海斯特夫人作证称，她认识赫格博士约一年；她经常见到他，并且他们已决定一同前往德国。他们将带上她年幼的女儿同行。旅费由赫格博士支付。尽管她就赫格博士是否有权接触其丈夫的黄金存放处这一问题接受了长时间讯问——这一事实若得到证实，将毫无疑问地给被告牙医定罪——但她坚决拒绝做出任何会牵连赫格博士的具体陈述。她证词的重要性未能显现，在经过一系列关于她拟与赫格博士同往德国的行程、她在青岛被捕以及随后被押解至此的常规提问后，她被允许退庭。
椅上受粗待
她的丈夫随后走上证人席作证称，当他成为被告的病人时，赫格博士“对待他很恶劣”。他说，有一次，在制作牙模的过程中，赫格博士猛地向后仰头，力度之大使他昏厥，并“认为”自己处于半意识状态。他作证说，正是在此时，他认为赫格博士拿走了他保险箱的钥匙，随后取走箱内物品，为与该女子及儿童逃往德国做准备。
后来，海斯特在与赫格的律师进行口头争辩时，激烈否认“整个案件是一场家庭纠纷，不应在法庭上审理”，以此显示此案使他情绪激动的程度。
在昨日的诉讼过程中，显而易见的是，检方的指控依赖于证明赫格博士曾持有海斯特保险箱的钥匙，并配制了一把用于非法进入的 duplicate key（复制钥匙）。然而，试图从证人那里获得能证明这一点的明确陈述的所有尝试均告失败。一名中国仆人或海斯特的密友也未能使赫格陷入绝境，因为结果发现他能作证的仅仅是他看到被告拿着一把“钥匙”这一事实。
警方此前的调查已证实，当那个男孩看到赫格博士时，他正在重配其邮政信箱的钥匙。案件定于3月5日继续审理。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 23, 1935
S. B. REGISTRY.

Heger Denies
Theft Charge
Before Court

Czech Dentist Admits
Taking German's Wife,
Child To Tsingtao Last
Month; Case Adjourned

"I'm Not A Thief, I'm
A Dentist," He Laughs

Dr. Vladimir Heger, 34-year-old Czechoslovakian who was deported from Japan as an "undesirable alien," upon being charged with stealing about $7,380 worth of gold and coins from Mr. F. Heister, a German residing in the Embankment Building, in the First Special District Court yesterday, denied any knowledge of the theft but admitted that he left Shanghai on January 10 accompanied by Mrs. Heister and her daughter.

During the course of the trial of Dr. Heger, who is a graduate of the Prague dental college, he was suspected of being the head of a "white slave" organization operating in the Far East.

Trial Adjourned

After a hearing in which the prosecution outlined the case and evidence was given by Mr. Heister, who is connected with Andersen, Meyer and Company, Limited, as well as the questioning of Dr. Heger by Judge Shiang, the trial was adjourned for a special session on the afternoon of March 1. A request was made by Mr. Ngai Tseng-ling, of the law firm of Paul Premet, appearing in behalf of Dr. Heger, that Mrs. Heister be called to testify in court as well as Dr. Korec, with whom Dr. Heger worked for a while after his arrival in Shanghai in April, 1933.

In outlining the case for the prosecution Mr. Tsiang said that on January 10, the Municipal Police were informed by Mr. Heister that about $8,000 worth of gold bars and other coins had been stolen from his desk in his apartment of 612 Embankment Building. At the time he suspected his wife, who with her daughter and Dr. Heger, it was discovered, sailed for Dairen that morning. The Tsingtao authorities were communicated with, Mrs. Heister was detained and sent back to Shanghai. No action was taken by Mr. Heister at the time and later he began suspecting Dr. Heger, who by that time was already in Harbin.

Fled To Japan

In Harbin, continued Mr. Tsiang, Dr. Heger came under the suspicion of the police as being a "white slaver" and immediately ran away to Japan, where he was arrested on January 13 and deported as an "undesirable alien."

Questioned by the judge, Dr. Heger admitted that on the morning of January 10 he left Shanghai with Mrs. Heister and her daughter. He stated that he had known both Mr. and Mrs. Heister since last year and that he met them when they came to him to have their teeth attended to. In reply to a question whether he admitted having stolen the gold from Mr. Heister, Dr. Heger replied with a laugh, "No, I didn't steal it; I am not a thief, I am a dentist."

In the course of his evidence, Dr. Heger stated that he had never visited Mr. Heister's apartment and that he only knew that the latter stayed in the Embankment Building, but did not know the apartment number.

Had A Key Made

Mr. Heister told the court that he suspected Dr. Heger had stolen the gold from him as he was told by Dr. Korec and a boy employed by Dr. Heger that Dr. Heger had been seen making a key similar to one which would fit the lock in his cabinet. Mr. Heister had to admit in reply to questions put by the defense that Dr. Heger had never visited his apartment as far as he knew.

In the end Mr. Heister, nervously told the court that his wife had not wanted to leave town, but that Dr. Heger had persuaded and hypnotized her to leave with him. According to Mr. Heister, Dr. Heger had intended to go to Germany via Siberia.

In closing the hearing until March 1, Judge Shiang ordered that Mrs. Heister be brought to court to testify at the next hearing. Mrs. Heister is staying with her husband.

赫格在法庭上
否认盗窃指控

捷克牙医承认上月
携德国人之妻及子女
前往青岛；案件延期审理

“我不是小偷，我是
牙医，”他笑道

弗拉基米尔·赫格医生（Dr. Vladimir Heger），34岁，捷克斯洛伐克人，此前曾作为“不受欢迎的外国人”被日本驱逐出境。昨日在第一特区法院被控从居住在堤岸大厦（Embankment Building）的德国人F. 海斯特先生（Mr. F. Heister）处窃取价值约7,380美元的金条和硬币时，他否认对盗窃案有任何知情，但承认他于今年1月10日随海斯特夫人及其女儿离开上海。

在赫格医生的审讯过程中，这位毕业于布拉格牙科学院的医生被怀疑是远东地区一个“白奴”组织的头目。

庭审延期

在控方概述案情、与安德森·迈耶有限公司（Andersen, Meyer and Company, Limited）有关联的海斯特先生提供证词，以及向法官香（Shiang，音译）对赫格医生进行讯问之后，庭审休庭，定于3月1日下午举行特别庭审。代表赫格医生出庭的保罗·普雷梅特（Paul Premet，音译）律师事务所的魏增龄（Ngai Tseng-ling，音译）先生提出请求，要求传唤海斯特夫人以及科雷克医生（Dr. Korec，音译）出庭作证；赫格医生于1933年4月抵达上海后，曾与科雷克医生共事过一段时间。

蒋（Tsiang，音译）先生在概述控方案情时表示，1月10日，市政警察接到海斯特先生报告，称其位于堤岸大厦612号公寓书桌内价值约8,000美元的金条和其他硬币被盗。当时他怀疑是其妻子所为，后经发现，其妻子携女儿与赫格医生于当日上午乘船前往大连。当局与青岛方面取得联系，海斯特夫人被扣留并遣返上海。海斯特先生当时未采取任何行动，后来他开始怀疑赫格医生，而彼时赫格医生已身在哈尔滨。

逃往日本

蒋先生继续说道，在哈尔滨，赫格医生因涉嫌从事“白奴”交易而受到警方怀疑，随即逃往日本，并于1月13日在那里被捕，随后作为“不受欢迎的外国人”被驱逐出境。

在接受法官讯问时，赫格医生承认他于1月10日上午与海斯特夫人及其女儿离开上海。他表示，自去年以来他就认识海斯特夫妇，是在他们前来就诊时相识的。当被问及是否承认从海斯特先生处窃取黄金时，赫格医生笑着回答：“不，我没有偷；我不是小偷，我是牙医。”

在作证过程中，赫格医生表示他从未去过海斯特先生的公寓，只知道后者住在堤岸大厦，但不知道具体的公寓门牌号。

配制钥匙

海斯特先生告诉法庭，他怀疑赫格医生偷了他的黄金，因为科雷克医生和赫格医生雇用的一名男孩告诉他，有人看见赫格医生配制了一把与其橱柜锁相配的钥匙。针对辩方提出的问题，海斯特先生不得不承认，据他所知，赫格医生从未去过他的公寓。

最后，海斯特先生紧张地告诉法庭，他的妻子本不愿离开上海，但赫格医生通过劝说和催眠使她随其离开。据海斯特先生称，赫格医生打算经西伯利亚前往德国。

在宣布休庭至3月1日之际，香法官命令将海斯特夫人带至法庭，在下次听证会上作证。海斯特夫人目前与其丈夫同住。

归档

Heger To Face
Charges Of
Larceny Today

Dentist Deported From
Japan As 'Undesirable'
Held By Hongkew Police

"White Slave" Charges
Originated In Harbin

Dr. Vladimir Heger, 34-year-old
Czechoslovakian, who was arrested
in Tokyo on February 13 suspected
of being the head of a "white slave"
organization operating in the Far
East, was brought to Shanghai
aboard the Shanghai Maru yesterday afternoon and will be charged
with larceny in the First Special
District Court this morning.

The Shanghai Maru was met by
International Settlement and Japanese Consular Police when she docked
yesterday afternoon. In accordance
with regular procedure Dr. Heger
who was deported from Japan as
an "undesirable alien," wanted
somewhere else, was taken off the
ship by the Japanese Consular
Police and handed over to the
Shanghai Municipal Police detectives, who immediately took him
to the Hongkew Police Station, as
the alleged larceny with which he
will be charged is said to have taken
place in the Embankment Building
on North Soochow Road.

Allegedly Stole Gold Bars
The Shanghai Municipal Police
have no information to the effect
that Dr. Heger, who is a graduate
of a Prague dental college, had
participated or had any connection
with the "white slave" traffic. The
only charge with which the local
police are at present concerned is
larceny and it is believed that the
white slavery allegations against the
man originated in Harbin. No official confirmation to the effect has
been received in Shanghai to date.
A warrant was sworn out in
Shanghai for the arrest of Dr.
Heger by Mr. F. Helster, employed
by Andersen, Meyer and Company,
Limited. Mr. Helster, it is understood, alleges that Dr. Heger stole
$60,000 worth of gold bars and
jewelry from his apartment in the
Embankment Building in the early
part of January.
It is also understood that on or
about January 15 after having
allegedly stolen the property Dr.
Heger accompanied by Mr. Helster's
wife left for Tientsin where they
stayed for a few days before proceeding to Peiping. From Peiping
they went to Mukden and thence
to Dairen where they boarded a
Japanese vessel for Kobe. At Kobe
Dr. Heger was arrested by the
Japanese police on a warrant issued
by the Czechoslovakian consul at
Kobe who had been requested to
do so by the Shanghai police.

Not Depressed
Dr. Heger seemed to be very confident when he arrived in Shanghai yesterday and was met by the
police. He was dressed in a new
camel hair coat and a brown velour
hat. He was clean shaven and had
a cheery outlook on life. Upon being taken to the Hongkew Police
Station by Detective-Sergeant F. O.
Guess, who is handling the case,
Dr. Heger had his two travelling
bags searched and was detained at
the station until such time as he
will be taken to court this morning.
It is understood that evidence
will be given this morning by both
Mr. and Mrs. Helster.
Dr. Heger apparently has led an
interesting life since he first arrived
here in August, 1933, without money
and with a diploma from the Czechoslovak school. Upon his arrival, he
met an Austrian doctor on Peking
Road who was charmed by the
Czech's apparent sincerity and zeal
for work. In addition, Dr. Heger
was recommended to the doctor by
the Czechoslovak consul, it was said.
The Peking Road doctor went to
the aid of the struggling young dentist, purchased equipment for him
and set up a dentist's office for him
in his own suite of offices.

Dr. Vladimir Heger

赫格尔今日
面临盗窃指控

牙医因“不受欢迎”
被日本驱逐
由虹口警方羁押

“白奴”指控
起源于哈尔滨

弗拉基米尔·赫格尔（Vladimir Heger）博士，34岁，捷克斯洛伐克人，于2月13日在东京被捕，涉嫌为在远东活动的“白奴”组织头目。昨日下午，他乘“上海丸”轮抵达上海，并将于今晨在第一特区地方法院被控犯有盗窃罪。

昨日下午“上海丸”轮靠岸时，国际租界警方和日本领事馆警察前往迎接。按照常规程序，赫格尔博士作为“不受欢迎的外国人”被日本驱逐，且在其他地方亦被通缉，因此由日本领事馆警察带离船只，移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探，后者随即将其带往虹口捕房，因为据称他将面临的盗窃指控发生于北苏州路的大厦（Embankment Building）。

涉嫌窃取金条
上海公共租界工部局警务处并无消息表明，毕业于布拉格牙科学校的赫格尔博士曾参与或与“白奴”贩卖活动有任何关联。当地警方目前关注的唯一指控是盗窃，据信针对此人的白奴贩卖指控起源于哈尔滨。截至目前，上海方面尚未收到对此事的官方证实。
受雇于安利洋行有限公司（Andersen, Meyer and Company, Limited）的F. 赫尔斯特（F. Helster）先生在上海宣誓签发逮捕赫格尔博士的拘票。据悉，赫尔斯特先生指控赫格尔博士于一月初从其位于大厦（Embankment Building）的公寓中窃取了价值6万美元的金条和珠宝。
另据悉，大约在1月15日，赫格尔博士在涉嫌窃取财物后，偕同赫尔斯特先生的妻子前往天津，在那里停留数日后前往北平。从北平他们去了沈阳，继而前往大连，在那里登上一艘开往神户的日轮。在神户，赫格尔博士被日本警方根据捷克斯洛伐克驻神户领事应上海警方请求签发的拘票逮捕。

并未消沉
赫格尔博士昨日抵达上海并由警方接待时，显得非常自信。他身穿一件新的驼毛大衣，头戴一顶棕色丝绒帽。他刮净了胡须，对生活持乐观态度。负责处理此案的警佐F. O. 格斯（F. O. Guess）将其带往虹口捕房时，赫格尔博士的两个旅行袋受到搜查，他被拘留在捕房，直至今晨被提堂。
据悉，赫尔斯特夫妇均将于今晨出庭作证。
自1933年8月身无分文、仅持一张捷克斯洛伐克学校文凭初抵此地以来，赫格尔博士显然过着一种有趣的生活。抵达后，他在北京路结识了一位奥地利医生，这位医生被这位捷克人表现出的真诚和工作热情所打动。此外，据说赫格尔博士还得到了捷克斯洛伐克领事的推荐。这位北京路的医生向这位 struggling 的年轻牙医伸出援手，为他购买了设备，并在自己的诊所套间内为他设立了一间牙科诊室。

弗拉基米尔·赫格尔博士

According to reports received
by the police from Harbin, the
deported man was alleged to be
at the head of an international

神户，2月19日电。— 一名自称弗拉基米尔·赫格尔（Vladimir Heger）的外国人今日作为“不受欢迎的外国人”被日本驱逐出境。他乘坐“上海丸”号轮船启程前往上海，据东京警方官员称，工部局警务处持有将其拘留的逮捕令。
一名东京警探正陪同该男子前往长崎，即该船停靠的最后一个日本港口。
该男子自称是捷克国籍，在上海设有牙科诊所，于2月8日因涉嫌贩卖白奴罪被东京警方拘留。
此次逮捕是基于哈尔滨警方提供的信息，称一名上海牙医逃避了他们的拘留并乘船前往日本。
由于该男子涉嫌犯下的罪行均非在日本境内实施，东京警察厅决定将其驱逐出境。
根据警方从哈尔滨收到的报告，被驱逐者据称是一个国际帮派的头目，该帮派向哈尔滨、上海和朝鲜北部的“妓院”提供年轻女孩。— 联合通讯社。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 15, 1935

Dentist Nabbed
In Tokyo Due
Here Shortly

Heger, Held In Connection
With White Slave Racket,
Did Business In Shanghai

Dr. Vladimir Heger, 34, a graduate of a Prague dental college now being held by Tokyo police on charges of participating in a gigantic "white slave" trafficking organization in the Orient, will be sent back to Shanghai in a few days when Tokyo police have completed their investigations, it was learned here yesterday.

Dr. Heger, a dentist, apparently has led an interesting life since he first arrived here in August, 1933, without money and with a diploma from the Czechoslovak school. Upon his arrival, he met an Austrian doctor on Peking Road who was charmed by the Czech's apparent sincerity and zeal for work. In addition, Dr. Heger was recommended to the doctor by the Czechoslovak consul, it was said. The Peking Road doctor went to the aid of the struggling young dentist, purchased equipment for him, and set up a dentist's office for him in his own suite of offices.

Had Strange Friends

"For a while Dr. Heger worked," his ex-friend told a CHINA PRESS reporter yesterday. "But later he brought in the strangest kinds of friends. Most of them were Russians. I was ashamed to have them in my office, but I said nothing.

"Finally, about five months ago, I broke completely with Dr. Heger. As far as I know, he set up another office on Nanking Road but didn't do much business. He lived in several places about the city. On about January 12 he left for Harbin and I haven't heard of him since until I read that he was held in Tokyo on a charge of 'white-slave' trafficking.

"Personally, I don't think Heger is for a minute guilty of that charge."

Arrested In Tokyo

Dr. Heger was arrested February 13 in Tokyo after he left Harbin where it is alleged the police were after him. A report appearing in a Harbin paper came to the attention of Tokyo police which stated that Dr. Heger was the head of a group of men German, Austrian, Czech, Russian and Portuguese who were connected with a large "white slave" racket in Shanghai and with branches in other cities.

（批：P.A. (Br. Br.) Passed by m. JMc FEB. 16/1935）

《字林西报》，1935年2月15日，星期五

牙医在东京被捕
不久将抵沪

赫格尔因涉及白奴勒索案
被拘，曾在上海执业

据悉，现年34岁的弗拉基米尔·赫格尔博士毕业于布拉格一所牙科学校，目前因参与东方巨大的“白奴”贩运组织而被东京警方拘留，待东京警方完成调查后，将于数日内被遣返上海。

赫格尔博士是一名牙医，自1933年8月身无分文、仅持一张捷克斯洛伐克学校文凭初抵此地以来，显然过着有趣的生活。据称，他抵达后结识了一位在北京路行医的奥地利医生，这位医生被这位捷克人表现出的真诚和工作热情所打动。此外，据说赫格尔博士还得到了捷克斯洛伐克领事的推荐。这位北京路的医生向这位 struggling 的年轻牙医伸出援手，为他购买了设备，并在自己的办公室套房内为他设立了一间牙科诊所。

结交奇怪的朋友

“赫格尔博士工作了一段时间，”他以前的朋友昨天告诉《字林西报》记者。“但后来他带来了一些最奇怪的朋友。他们大多是俄国人。我为让他们出现在我的办公室里感到羞愧，但我什么也没说。

“最后，大约五个月前，我与赫格尔博士彻底决裂。据我所知，他在南京路另设了一间诊所，但生意不多。他在市内几处地方居住。大约在1月12日，他前往哈尔滨，此后我便没有他的消息，直到我看到新闻说他因涉嫌‘白奴’贩运在东京被拘。

“就我个人而言，我不认为赫格尔有一秒钟是有罪的。”

在东京被捕

赫格尔博士于2月13日在东京被捕，此前他离开了哈尔滨，据称那里警方正在追捕他。引起东京警方注意的是一份出现在哈尔滨报纸上的报道，该报道指出赫格尔博士是一个由德国人、奥地利人、捷克人、俄国人和葡萄牙人组成的团伙的头目，该团伙与上海的一个大型“白奴”勒索案有关，并在其他城市设有分支。

（批注：P.A. (英籍英国人) m. JMc 审阅 1935年2月16日）

MISCELLANEOUS

MAINICHI

SHANGHAI DENTIST ARRESTED IN TOKYO FOR BEING THE
HEAD OF AN INTERNATIONAL WHITE SLAVE GANG

A Rengo telegram from
Tokyo dated February 13 states that according to a
report published on February 2 in a Russian newspaper
in Harbin, a white slave gang was organized in the
Far East during the past two years with headquarters
in Shanghai. Recently a branch was established in
Harbin. The gang succeeded in abducting several women
who were sold to certain persons in South China. The
gang is endeavouring to abduct more women in order to
send them to Ranan(Korea), Java, Shanghai and Chefoo.
About ten men of various nationality such as Austrians,
Germans, Czechoslovkians, Swedes and Portuguese are
engaged in the activities and they abduct women under
the pretext of marriage. A dental surgeon named
Heger, the head of the gang, was staying at the Modern
Hotel, Harbin, but on February 2 he left owing to the
fact that the Police in Harbin were searching for him.
The centre figure in the activities is an Austrian
named Jibev(?). Several white Russian women are reported
to have been victimized.

Acting on the newspaper report,
the Foreign Section of the Tokyo Police which was making
inquiries regarding the affair arrested a Czechoslovakian
named Vuragimil Heger, age 34, who registered at the
Bankei Hotel, Tokyo, on February 5. The prisoner
admitted to the police that he left Shanghai for Harbin
on February 1 because the Shanghai Police were shadowing
him, and that he left Harbin for Japan with Yen 1,500
because the Harbin Police wanted to arrest him. The
prisoner further stated that he has a dental office at No.
83 Nanking Road, Shanghai and was formerly a Major
in the Czechoslovakian Army.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 14, 1935

ALLEGED TRAFFIC IN
WHITE SLAVES

Arrest In Tokyo Of a
Man Claiming To
Be Dentist

TOKYO, Feb. 13.—A foreigner
who said that he was a Shanghai
dentist, was detained by the
police to-day at Mampei Hotel,
on a charge of 'white slave'
trafficking.
Following the arrest, the police
declared that the detained man
was the head of an international
"white slave" gang, operating in
Manchuria, Japan and China.
The man, according to the
police, said that he had served in
the army as a sub-lieutenant of
infantry.
The police said that their sus-
picions were first aroused by a
report in a Harbin Russian daily
on February 2 of the activities
of a "white slave" gang, having
its headquarters in Shanghai and
branches in Harbin and other
towns in the Orient. The report
said that the gang employed
more than 12 young men of Ger-
man, Austrian, Czech, Swiss and
Portuguese nationalities to marry
young Russian girls and later
sell them to Shanghai, Java, Che-
foo and Ranan (Korea) "houses."
The newspaper report added
that the leader of the gang, a
dentist, left the Hotel Moderne in
Harbin very hurriedly when the
police tried to question him.
Learning of the arrival of a
dentist from Harbin, the Tokyo
Metropolitan Police questioned
him and reportedly found that he
was the person mentioned by the
Harbin newspaper.
The police say that the man
confessed that he arrived in Har-
bin from Shanghai, but that the
action of the Harbin police drove
him to Tokyo, where he arrived
with Y.1,500 in cash.—Rengo.

涉嫌贩卖
白奴

一名自称
牙医的男子
在东京被捕

东京，2月13日电。— 一名自称是上海
牙医的外国人，今日在万平酒店被警方
以“白奴”贩运罪名拘留。
逮捕发生后，警方宣称，被拘留男子
是一个在满洲、日本和中国活动的国际
“白奴”帮派的头目。
据警方称，该男子表示他曾
在军队中担任步兵少尉。
警方表示，他们的怀疑最初是由2月2日
哈尔滨一家俄文日报关于一个“白奴”帮派
活动的报道引起的，该帮派总部设在
上海，并在哈尔滨及东方其他城镇设有
分支。报道称，该帮派雇佣了
12多名德国、奥地利、捷克、瑞士和
葡萄牙国籍的年轻男子，与年轻的俄国
女孩结婚，随后将她们卖到上海、爪哇、芝
罘和罗南（朝鲜）的“妓院”。
该报纸报道还补充说，当警方
试图讯问该帮派头目（一名牙医）时，
他匆忙离开了哈尔滨的现代酒店。
得知一名来自哈尔滨的牙医抵达后，
东京警视厅对其进行了讯问，据称发现他
就是哈尔滨报纸提到的那个人。
警方称，该男子供认他是从上海抵达哈

前往东京，他抵达时随身携带了1,500
日元现金。— 联合通讯社。
